tagline: A leading next-generation technology services provider combining innovative technologies and deep industry expertise with an AI-native approach to drive digital transformation
hero_kpi_rationale: Endava is undergoing a comprehensive strategic transformation toward an 'AI-native' approach, positioning its current investments as a key driver of its future growth in next-generation technology services.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: Quarterly revenue amounts to £184.1 million, down 5.9% year-on-year, but showing sequential growth.
kpis.signal: Revenue down year-on-year, but sequential growth of 3.3%.

kpis.name: Adjusted PBT Margin
kpis.explanation: Adjusted profit before tax expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: The adjusted margin for fiscal year 2025 stands at 10.6%, compared to 11.2% the previous year, impacted by strategic investments in AI transformation.
kpis.signal: Adjusted margin stable at 10.6% for fiscal year 2025, but down from 11.2% the prior year, reflecting investments in AI-native transformation.

kpis.name: Adjusted EPS
kpis.explanation: Adjusted earnings per share, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EPS declined to £0.16 from £0.30 a year earlier, due to transformation-related costs and margin pressure.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EPS sharply lower despite strategic investments in AI transformation.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees at the end of the period.
kpis.description: Average operational headcount decreased by 1.7% in fiscal year 2025, from 11,668 to 11,385 employees, due to adjustments made in response to macroeconomic conditions.
kpis.signal: Slight reduction in headcount reflecting adjustments related to macroeconomic conditions.

kpis.name: Adjusted Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after investments, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted FCF declined to £20.1 million from £31.6 million a year earlier.
kpis.signal: Adjusted FCF significantly lower, driven by margin pressure and macroeconomic conditions.

kpis.name: Clients Generating Over £1M
kpis.explanation: Number of clients generating more than one million pounds sterling over the last 12 months.
kpis.description: The number of clients with annual spend of at least £1.0 million was 133 in fiscal year 2025, down from 146 in fiscal year 2024, reflecting the challenging environment for next-generation IT services.
kpis.signal: Loss of premium clients in fiscal year 2025 (133 vs 146 in 2024), reflecting macroeconomic headwinds affecting technology services.

kpis.name: Top 10 Clients Concentration
kpis.explanation: Percentage of annual revenue generated by the top 10 clients.
kpis.description: No single client contributed more than 10% of revenue in fiscal year 2025. The top 10 clients generated an average of £27.9 million per client, compared to £24.1 million the prior year.
kpis.signal: Client concentration relatively stable, with no client representing more than 10% of revenue in fiscal year 2025.

kpis.name: Annual Revenue FY2025
kpis.explanation: Total revenue for fiscal year 2025 ended June 30, 2025.
kpis.description: Total revenue for fiscal year 2025 amounted to £772.3 million, up 4.3% from £740.8 million the prior year. On a constant currency basis, growth reached 6.3%.
kpis.signal: 4.3% reported revenue growth, but slight three-year CAGR decline to 1.4% due to currency pressure.

kpis.name: AI Native Pivot
kpis.explanation: Significant investments in AI hiring, training, and partnerships to transform technology service offerings.
kpis.description: Endava is making substantial investments to become a leader in 'AI-native' technology services, combining innovative technologies with deep domain expertise.
kpis.signal: Deep transformation of the company's DNA toward AI-native, integrating AI across every phase of the customer lifecycle.

kpis.name: Dava.Flow Launch
kpis.explanation: New AI-native engagement lifecycle to help clients accelerate growth and solve complex challenges.
kpis.description: Dava.Flow represents Endava's new AI-native engagement lifecycle, offering a turnkey solution for client digital transformations with an AI-native approach.
kpis.signal: Flagship product of Endava's AI transformation showing strong initial client interest, key to future differentiation.

kpis.name: Active Clients
kpis.explanation: Total number of active clients generating revenue over the last 12 months.
kpis.description: The active client base totaled 619 clients in fiscal year 2025 (as of June 30, 2025), down from 695 in 2024 and 711 in 2023, due to macroeconomic headwinds.
kpis.signal: Client base contraction (619 vs 695 in 2024) reflecting macroeconomic challenges affecting demand for technology services.

risks.title: Dependence on Client Perception of Value
risks.summary: Endava's ability to maintain favorable pricing depends heavily on the perceived value added by its services. A decline in this perception or increased competitive pressure could reduce its margins and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is highlighted centrally in the 10-K, with strong language on direct impact to profitability. The trend is stable, but increased competitive pressure reinforces this risk. The Competition category is strategic for Endava.

risks.title: Cybersecurity Threats to Sensitive Data and Systems
risks.summary: Endava collects and processes sensitive data (client, IP, trade secrets). A breach of its systems or those of third parties could result in financial losses, litigation, and reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned high in the document, with alarming language ('adverse consequences'), rising trend in cyber threats, and critical exposure to client data. Cybersecurity is a major regulatory and operational priority.

risks.title: Dependence on Skilled Technology Talent
risks.summary: Endava relies heavily on its ability to recruit and retain highly qualified IT professionals. A talent shortage or rising wage costs could harm its profitability and growth.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned multiple times, with strong emphasis on the difficulty of attracting and retaining IT professionals. Trend is stable but critical. This category is central for a technology services provider.

risks.title: Risks Associated with Generative Artificial Intelligence Use
risks.summary: Endava uses generative AI tools in its operations. Their operational inefficiency, biases, or undetected errors could lead to losses, legal liability, and reputational harm.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in key risks, with cautious but concerned language ('operational challenges, liability'). Trend is rising with AI adoption. The Technology category is rapidly evolving.

risks.title: Increased Competition and Technological Innovation
risks.summary: If Endava fails to innovate and keep pace with emerging technology trends, it risks losing clients to more agile or better-positioned competitors offering new solutions.
risks.score_rationale: Highly positioned among risks, with strong language ('lose clients and not remain competitive'). Trend is rising with accelerating technology. The Technology category is critical for differentiation.

risks.title: Dependence on Open-Source and Third-Party Software
risks.summary: Endava integrates open-source software and third-party technologies into its deliverables. Poor license management or defects in these components could harm client projects and expose the company to liability.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned with moderate intensity but real impact. Trend is stable. Dependence on third-party components is common but can lead to failures or license violations.

risks.title: Strict Data Protection Regulations
risks.summary: Endava is subject to strict privacy and data security regulations, particularly in the EU and UK. Actual or perceived non-compliance could result in fines, litigation, and client loss.
risks.score_rationale: Positioned very high, with alarming language ('stringent and evolving laws'), trend rising with GDPR strengthening and other regimes. The Regulation category is critical in Europe and the UK.

risks.title: Dependence on Key Industry Verticals
risks.summary: A significant portion of Endava's revenue comes from a few vertical sectors. A decline in demand in one of these sectors or an inability to enter new markets could harm its results.
risks.score_rationale: Clearly mentioned in risks, with concerned language ('adversely affect'). Trend is stable. Sector concentration amplifies the risk of demand decline in a major vertical.

ai_positioning.summary: Endava positions itself as a leader in next-generation technology services with an 'AI-native' approach. The company is undergoing a comprehensive strategic transformation by integrating AI into every phase of the customer lifecycle, combining innovative technologies with deep domain expertise to accelerate client growth and solve complex challenges.
evidence: Significant investments in AI hiring and training to develop AI-native capabilities
Launch of Dava.Flow, a new AI-native client engagement lifecycle
Expanded strategic partnerships in the AI ecosystem and integration of AI into every client solution
Growth in the Healthcare vertical (11.8% of revenue in FY2025, up 5.7 points vs FY2024) demonstrating diversification

events.title: TaskUs (TASK) Q1 Earnings Miss Estimates
events.body: TaskUs (TASK) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of -1.41% and +3.50%, respectively, for the quarter ended March 2026. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?
